pos.personaBrief: Diniz's Flu had about 70% possession in the Libertadores final, committed to build-up even when 1-0 up (TSG), and says 'I like having the ball'. Possession is its identity and defence.

pro.personaBrief: Short-pass build-up from the keeper with André dropping between centre-backs (TSG, TFA, IstoE), 'coragem para jogar' even under pressure; patient circulation and rotation, not directness.

est.personaBrief: Self-described 'aposicional', no fixed positions, 7-8 players clustered near the ball, rotations, full-backs inside, centre-backs roaming (Sky, Trivela, Netflu, NYT).

lar.personaBrief: Both wingers often on the same flank with one-twos, full-backs inside between lines, overload then switch; Keno gives width only occasionally. Play is close-combination, not crossing-based.

blo.personaBrief: PPDA 7.33, forwards press from goal kick, high line, block advancing, immediate counter-press (CV, TFA, TSG, Blizzard). Presses build-up rather than dropping.

mar.personaBrief: Marking is an open question; hints of zone-oriented handovers (wrong switch by Marcelo) and no dedicated man-marker, with space-protecting compactness around the ball.

pla.personaBrief: Dinizismo is a fixed identity played whoever the opponent, kept even against Man City; he did tweak for Olimpia and imposes his model on players, adjusting details at half-time rather than the plan.

res.personaBrief: Courage to play, 'sem sair de seu estilo' even in the Club World Cup final loss to City; did not add a centre-back when winning the final; style is valued, though he also won the Libertadores.

sis.personaBrief: Collective fluidity is the core (NYT: team of the future), yet Ganso is the maestro and individuals are encouraged to solve problems freely; everyone presses and works in the collective.

jog.personaBrief: Technical players (Ganso, Andre, Arias, Keno, Marcelo) fit the aposicional game; classic playmaker Ganso is the maestro, though training is war-like and pressing is intense.

bas.personaBrief: Veterans Fabio, Felipe Melo, Ganso, Marcelo, Keno anchor the team, while young John Kennedy and Lelê got trust; squad built via signings, not academy-first.

lid.personaBrief: Psychology graduate, motivator who cares for players like John Kennedy, uses rest days, training described as war; people-centred and collaborative over iron-fist rules.
